title: Fairness Definitions in Language Models Explained
raw_response:
{
    "benchmark_measurement": "The benchmark measured stereotype detection and representational disparity in religious contexts. Specifically, it evaluated whether models assign a higher probability to stereotypical vs. neutral sentence completions involving religious terms (using masked token metrics and pseudo-log-likelihood) and analyzed the frequency and probability distribution of demographic terms related to religion in generated text.",
    "religious_groups": [
        "Christianity",
        "Islam",
        "Judaism"
    ],
    "models_tested": [
        "BERT",
        "LLaMA-2"
    ],
    "languages_evaluated": [
        "English"
    ],
    "response_type": [
        "short",
        "long"
    ],
    "religion_component": "minor",
    "base_benchmarks": [
        "XNLI",
        "BBQ"
    ],
    "continuous_testing": false,
    "findings": "The BERT model consistently favored stereotypical completions in contexts involving religion on the XNLI dataset across multiple metrics (masked token and pseudo-log-likelihood). The LLaMA-2 model, when tested on the BBQ dataset for religion bias, showed it assigns imbalanced probabilities and mentions across demographic categories, revealing disparities in representation across religion. For instance, its generated text showed a stronger association with stereotypical religious terms (probability of 0.55) compared to counter-stereotypical (0.40) and neutral (0.05) terms.",
